interface.title: Light curve inspector and labeler
interface.field: Astronomy: time-domain photometry of periodic variable stars
interface.stage_of_work: Data curation and labeling: building a training set or catalog by classifying candidate periodic variables, alone or with several people labeling the same set (collaborative or crowd-sourced labeling)
interface.what_it_is_for: Shows survey light curves of variable stars nine to a page, each folded at the reported period and at twice that period, so a person can label each one RR Lyrae, Eclipsing Binary, Cepheid or Other. Several people can label the same set under separate usernames. The output is one label array per user, saved as resultfolder/<username>/backup.pkl (-1 means unlabeled) and restored at that user's next log-in.

data.note: The server was started with its own folder of light curves (files like lc_b201_23338.dat with reported periods of about 0.44–0.75 days). It holds 18 curves (0–17), shown on pages 0 and 1. The counter shows a 0-based page number against the page count, so 'Page 1 out of 2' is the last page. Nothing was uploaded. The run used a 1700 px wide browser window so the plot toolbar was not cut off; this was a harness setup step, not a user step.

features.name: Paged small-multiples grid with a moving highlight
features.general: Show a batch of items as a grid of small charts, mark the current item with a coloured frame, move that marker through the batch and on to the next, and jump to the first item not yet done
features.specific: 3x3 grid of folded light curves, each titled with index, file and period. A red frame marks the highlighted curve. Labeling moves it on; the ninth label opens the next page; Previous/Next page keep the same grid slot; a 'Page N out of M' counter (N 0-based) shows where you are; Find first unlabeled goes to the page and curve of the first curve without a class.
steps: Open the grid; item 0 is highlighted
Label or step to move the highlight to the next plot
After the last plot, the next page of 9 loads by itself
Use Previous page / Next page to move between pages, keeping the grid slot
Read the page counter (0-based page number out of the page count)
Press Find first unlabeled to jump to the first item without a label
serves_tasks: Move to the next batch once the current one is done
Go back and forth between batches by hand
Jump to the first item still without a label

features.name: One-click class buttons with undo-by-step
features.general: Label the current item with a fixed set of class buttons; each click writes the label onto the item and moves on, and a back button lets you redo the previous one
features.specific: RR Lyrae / Eclipsing Binary / Cepheid / Other buttons add 'Class: …' to the highlighted plot's title and move to the next curve. Go back one moves the highlight back, across page boundaries too, so a new click replaces the old label.
steps: Look at the highlighted plot
Click a class button; the label shows in the title and the highlight moves on
Press Go back one to return to the previous item, even on the previous page
Click a different class to replace the label
serves_tasks: Assign a class to the current item and move to the next
Correct a label you already gave, even if it was in the previous batch

features.name: Dual-period folded light curve plot
features.general: Plot a periodic time series folded at a candidate period and at twice that period, side by side on the same axes in two colours, so the true period can be judged
features.specific: Each plot shows phase 0–2 in red (folded at the reported period, one cycle per unit of phase) and phase 2–4 in blue (folded at twice the reported period), with magnitude error bars. The legend text in the side panel has the colours backwards (it calls blue the reported period and red twice the period).
steps: Read the file name and reported period in the title
Compare the red fold (reported period, phase 0–2) with the blue fold (twice the period, phase 2–4); ignore the reversed legend
If the twice-period fold shows two unequal minima, the true period is twice the reported one, as for an eclipsing binary; if its two halves match, the reported period stands, as for an RR Lyrae
Pick the class from that judgement
serves_tasks: Judge the quality and shape of a periodic signal by eye
Assign a class to the current item and move to the next

features.name: Per-plot zoom/pan/reset/save toolbar
features.general: Zoom into or move around one chart of a grid using a shared toolbar, return it to its starting view, and export the charts as images
features.specific: Bokeh's default toolbar above the grid: Pan, Box Zoom (affects only the plot dragged on), Reset, and Save (downloads one bokeh_plot.png per plot, 9 in all)
steps: Choose Box Zoom and drag a box over one plot
Choose Pan and drag to move along phase
Press Reset to return to the starting view (after a page change this restores page 0's axis ranges, a bug)
Press Save to download a PNG of each plot
serves_tasks: Judge the quality and shape of a periodic signal by eye

features.name: Per-user resumable labeling session
features.general: Log in with a name, have your labels saved under that name and restored next time, so several people can label the same set separately
features.specific: Log in with just a username. Labels are backed up to resultfolder/<username>/backup.pkl only when labeling the ninth curve on a page moves you to the next page (Previous/Next page do not save), and are restored on the next log-in. A different username starts with no labels.
steps: Type a username and press Ready
Label every curve on a page; the ninth label moves to the next page and writes the backup
Leave, reload, and log in again as the same name; saved labels come back
Labels on the last page are never backed up, since there is no next page to move to
A different username starts with no labels
serves_tasks: Identify yourself so your labels are kept apart from other people's
Resume a labeling session after leaving
Start a separate session as a different person labeling the same set
